license: Original code and fixtures authored for this evaluation. No upstream source file is copied into this package. The behaviour contract comes from the documented Windows I/O completion port model: a handle is associated with a port together with a completion key, finished overlapped operations are queued as packets carrying that key, and waiting threads draw packets atomically so that one packet is delivered to exactly one thread (MSDN: CreateIoCompletionPort, GetQueuedCompletionStatus).
lineage: Documented Windows completion-port semantics (per-handle completion keys handed back by the kernel, atomic packet delivery to exactly one waiting thread, WAIT_TIMEOUT when the port is empty) -> workspace module wciocp frozen in the naive shape that keeps finished operations in a process-local list which every waiter scans -> Windows completion contract expressed as acceptance criteria A-G -> evaluator-side independent measurement: the grader creates its own overlapped objects, registers distinct completion keys, submits its own reads, and draws packets from several threads at once, checking that every request comes back exactly once with the key that was registered for it -> local oracle/no-change differential calibration -> container control runs on the pinned Windows Server Core image.
pollution_risk: Low. The subject is Windows I/O completion ports: handle-to-port association with a completion key, kernel-queued completion packets, atomic single-consumer delivery and WAIT_TIMEOUT. A dedup sweep over all 159 records of the procurement Base for the keywords CreateIoCompletionPort, GetQueuedCompletionStatus, IOCP, 完成端口, 完成键, OVERLAPPED, 重叠 I/O, CancelIoEx, 句柄继承, STARTUPINFOEX, 稀疏文件, VirtualQueryEx, PE/COFF and 注册表变更通知 returned no hit for the completion-port family; the occupied neighbouring families are sparse-file allocation (215), virtual address space (216), handle inheritance (218), per-request cancellation (219), file identity and hard links, Job Objects, reparse points and reserved device names. Python's own asyncio/select surface cannot express a completion key handed back by the kernel, so a relabelled duplicate of an existing task is not possible.
authorization: No external repository is vendored. The only third-party artefacts are the pinned Microsoft Windows Server Core base image, the PSF-licensed Python 3.12.9 embeddable distribution, MinGit and the offline wheelhouse already used by the other tasks in this batch. No network access is required to build or grade the task.
